body:
That is inconsistent with many other "polygon draw" related Nodes and classes that also all start in "add" mode or at least switch to it when their data array is empty. It would also make the feature hard to discover for newer users.

This should be solved by actually making the move mode when selected in the editor toolbar override the behavior, not switching the default, else you would basically just trade your annoyance for other peoples annoyance by changing the behavior.

> That is inconsistent with many other "polygon draw" True for `CollisionPolygon3D` too. If we are talking about the polygon editing inconsistencies in 3d there are many. `CollisionPolygon3D`, `CSGPolygon3D`, and `OccluderInstance3D` have the same polygon editing tool. But `NavigationObstacle3D` has a different one. `OccluderInstance3D` doesn't enable any editing until you set a `PolygonOccluder3D` as an occluder resource. `CSGPolygon3D` comes with a predefined cube shape so it has edit mode enabled by default which doesn't break the flow of working with 3d. `Path3D` doesn't have a problem of flow breakage because it has its mode set to "select mode" by default. Based on these findings I wouldn't say that editor flow breakage is consistent in all 3d nodes that support any kind of polygon or curve drawing. It is consistent in a way that all of these nodes have a polygon/curve editing mode but all of them behave differently. The problem is also exacerbated by the fact that when you add a `CollisionPolygon3D` or a `NavigationObstacle3D` node it usually doesn't add it to the place you need it to be because it adds a node with a local zero coordinates. In fact if you would postpone the creation of the polygon you would get into the same trap of getting into the polygon creation mode just by selecting the node which is not consistent with other 3d nodes that prevent you from using the editor viewport by default just by having them selected. > This should be solved by actually making the move mode when selected in the editor toolbar override the behavior, not switching the default, else you would basically just trade your annoyance for other peoples annoyance by changing the behavior. I'm not sure what "move mode" is... If you are talking about making a third option that fully disables any interactions with the polygon then that could eliminate the problem if it's selected by default. Which could also help with situations when the transform gizmo overlaps with the polygon points and you don't know if you are going to move a polygon point or change the transform of the whole node:

> I'm not sure what "move mode" is...

The editor toolbar to the left has different modes, e.g. select, transform, ... it makes the intention clear what a user currently wants to do for tools, so plugins can react to that and don't need to guess if a user wants to transform-move the node or select / edit it.
